title: Inference hosting controls and log minimization sync - Quartz Labs
summary: Discovery covering hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), log minimization and redaction, KMS/HSM and key residency concerns, legal hold / e-discovery needs, and next steps to provide security docs and a minimal retention POC. Customer is security-first and leaning to dedicated or private for production; interested in a short pilot on hosted with strict log redaction to prove flow.
next_steps: Marcus to share Redwood security whitepaper + SOC2 report link by 2026-05-14
Priya to propose a pilot config for hosted log-minimization (sample retention + redaction rules) by 2026-05-19
Quartz to confirm legal retention/e-discovery window and provide example PII fields by 2026-05-18
Schedule SE deep-dive bench/runbook session to test redaction latency impact (30-45m) week of 2026-05-25
action_items: Priya: build a sample hosted log redaction policy and demo dataset (due 2026-05-19)
Marcus: send SOC2 + infosec packet + network diagram (due 2026-05-14)
Evan: share list of regulatory controls we must evidence (GDPR articles, internal retention policy) (due 2026-05-18)
Samir: confirm whether legal hold can be scoped to specific queries vs full tenant capture (due 2026-05-20)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Delgado (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Quartz Head of Security), Maya Li (Quartz Platform Eng), Samir Khan (Quartz Legal)

[00:00] Marcus: cool, uh, everyone, thanks for joining, um, i'll do a quick intro from our side, this is Marcus from Redwood AE, and Priya's our SE who will nerd out on the infra stuff. can you do quick intros on quartz side?
[00:12] Evan: yeah hi i'm Evan, head of security at Quartz, responsible for infra and compliance for our inference stack.
[00:17] Maya: Maya, platform team. i'm the person who will actually run the connectors and do the deploys.
[00:20] Samir: Samir, legal counsel, i'll be focused on retention and e-discovery requirements.
[00:24] Marcus: awesome. objective today is to go over hosting options and, importantly, log minimization and residency controls. we know you mentioned gdpr and a couple of finance controls in the RFP. quick high level: are you exploring hosted first or are you leaning dedicated/private?
[00:38] Evan: short answer, we want a hosted pilot to start because it's fast, but production probably has to be dedicated or private — our compliance binds us to restrict logs and have key residency.
[00:46] Priya: totally understood. when you say restrict logs, can you walk me through what you mean — is it retention window, redaction, scrub before it leaves region, or full mailbox audit?
[00:56] Evan: primarily retention and redaction. we need PII elements stripped or hashed before leaving our region; also audit trails that show who queried what when for legal hold. for gdpr we need the ability to delete data upon subject request.
[01:10] Samir: and add legal hold: if there's litigation we may need to snapshot interactions tied to a case. that has to be preserved even if retention window says otherwise.
[01:19] Marcus: ok. on Redwood side we have a couple of controls: hosted API can be configured with minimal logging, prefix/KV caching can be disabled, and we offer per-tenant retention policies; dedicated gives you reserved pools and more control over logs and network egress; private gives you the control plane in your VPC or on-prem so logs never touch Redwood-managed storage.
[01:36] Maya: can you be specific about where logs land in hosted? are they in Redwood S3 in us-east-1, and can they be encrypted with our KMS?
[01:44] Priya: good q. hosted by default stores application logs in our encrypted storage in the region you pick. we support customer-managed keys via KMS for dedicated and private — for hosted we can discuss CMK support depending on the agreement; many customers opt for dedicated when they require CMK-only for audit.
[02:02] Evan: that's the crux. our policy says customer keys for any stored model artifacts or logs containing PII. otherwise we need to show controls to the board.
[02:11] Marcus: understood. one option is a hosted pilot but with log minimization: we can configure the pipeline to redact fields client-side before sending, or we can enable server-side redaction rules to scrub tokens that match regexes. both have pros/cons (client-side is safest but requires work on your side).
[02:28] Maya: client-side is appealing but our product team worries about latency and UX if we pre-process every prompt. can you quantify the latency hit for server-side redaction?
[02:36] Priya: from our experiments, basic regex redaction adds a couple of ms per request but heavy NLP redaction (PII detection models) can add 20-80ms depending on sequence length. we can push redaction into the pipeline asynchronously for logs — so main inference path isn't blocked, but then you lose immediate guarantee of redaction before storage.
[02:55] Evan: that asynchronous model worries us; we need to ensure that nothing unredacted persists, even transiently, because of GDPR and internal policy.
[03:03] Marcus: fair. we also support a storeless mode where we don't persist full request/response payloads for hosted customers; instead we store only minimal metadata for billing and tracing. that can be coupled with a short retention for telemetry (e.g., 24-72 hours) and immediate redaction.
[03:18] Samir: what's in "minimal metadata"? phone home traces? does that include the prompt hash?
[03:23] Priya: typically request id, model id, token counts, latency, status codes, and a prompt hash (cryptographic). the hash cannot be reversed to original prompt. we also allow customers to opt out of prompt hashing for additional privacy.
[03:34] Maya: i like the hash idea; but our compliance requires we can link a request to a tenant or user id for audits. can tenant/user correlation be preserved without storing the content?
[03:44] Priya: yes — you can map the request id to your tenant id in your local logs; Redwood can store the request id and not the payload. that allows correlation while keeping content out of Redwood storage.
[03:53] Evan: and about legal hold — if we need to snapshot an interaction, can that be done on-demand and exported under customer-managed encryption?
[04:00] Marcus: yes for dedicated/private we support export under customer CMK. for hosted we can run an export and encrypt it with a temporary key and provide the bundle; CMK-in-hosted requires a contract addendum in many cases.
[04:12] Samir: is there an audit trail showing who triggered the export and when? we need that for chain-of-custody.
[04:18] Priya: audit events are logged with actor identity, timestamp, and operation (export, delete, key-rotation). in dedicated/private the audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (syslog or cloud ingestion).
[04:30] Maya: on encryption: you said CMK support for dedicated and private. for private (VPC) do we need an HSM or can we bring our cloud KMS?
[04:38] Priya: you can bring your cloud KMS; we also integrate with HSMs for escrow if you have regulatory requirement for hardware-backed keys.
[04:45] Evan: is there any notion of key escrow or third-party key escrow for cross-jurisdictional audits?
[04:50] Marcus: yes we offer key escrow options for enterprise — e.g., escrow with a neutral custodian; that tends to be part of enterprise licensing.
[04:58] Maya: okay, switching to residency — if our users in eu call the API, can we force all data to remain in eu region?
[05:05] Priya: yes — when you provision, you choose region and we pin storage and inference to that region for dedicated/private. for hosted we have region selection but fallback to other regions if capacity constrained unless you enable region lock which is an add-on.
[05:20] Evan: region lock add-on — does that include contractual guarantees and penalties?
[05:24] Marcus: enterprise contract yes, with SLAs and clear fallback rules.
[05:28] Samir: what about logs copied for internal debugging or if your SREs need to look at a request? are those restricted?
[05:33] Priya: access is role-based; only authorized engineers with just-in-time access can access request content. we also provide redaction-at-rest for logs and automatic masking for developer debug flows. all access is audited.
[05:45] Evan: how often do Redwood SREs need to access payloads in practice?
[05:48] Priya: rare — most support uses metadata and request-replay with sanitized inputs. when we need actual payloads it's usually for production incidents and we require customer approval or legal binding (for enterprise).
[06:00] Maya: there's a technical detail: our models use KV cache. are those cached keys stored in plaintext anywhere? we cannot have raw conversational state exfiltrated.
[06:08] Priya: KV cache is ephemeral in-memory on the serving nodes; we do not persist raw KV cache to long-term storage. however, we may snapshot some state for debugging if explicit permission given.
[06:19] Evan: are those serving nodes multi-tenant for hosted? is there risk of cross-tenant leakage?
[06:24] Priya: good question — hosted uses multi-tenant pools but with strict isolation: process-level separation, tokenization boundaries, and dedicated memory isolation primitives. that said, customers with strict non-sharing requirements use dedicated or private to remove multi-tenant surface.
[06:38] Marcus: important callout: for PCI / financial controls, many banks prefer dedicated because it reduces attack surface and makes audits simpler. we have a checklist we can share.
[06:48] Samir: please do. also, about legal hold and e-discovery: can we scope retention to specific queries (like only support requests tagged to a case) rather than full tenant dumps?
[06:58] Priya: yes, we support targeted preservation. you can tag interactions with your internal case-id and Redwood's retention policy can be applied per-tag. that lets you snapshot only relevant interactions.
[07:08] Evan: fantastic. one more operational: we use strict data minimization. can Redwood redact entity types using an NLP model (names, emails) rather than naive regex?
[07:18] Priya: yes, Redwood supports ML-driven PII detection and redaction pipelines; they're heavier but are better at catching edge cases. we can provide a sample run on your sample dataset to show recall/precision tradeoffs.
[07:31] Maya: what's the false positive risk? we can't over-redact or we'll lose signal.
[07:35] Priya: typically precision is high for emails/SSNs, lower for names (context matters). we'll tune rules by combining regex + ML; customers often configure a conservative rule set for legal and a lighter one for analytics.
[07:48] Evan: about telemetry retention windows: can we set host retention to 24 hours for hosted pilot and then move to 90 days for dedicated?
[07:57] Marcus: yes that's common. our hosted pilot templates often use 24-72 hours; dedicated allows custom longer windows.
[08:04] Samir: is there an immutable tamper-proof log for audit events? we need chain-of-custody, so SHA-based append-only logs or forward to our SIEM are preferable.
[08:14] Priya: we can forward audit events to your SIEM in near real-time. we also support WORM-style storage for audit trails on dedicated/private if needed.
[08:24] Maya: for the pilot, we want to test redaction quality and measure latency impact. what's the best approach?
[08:30] Marcus: recommendation: short hosted pilot with sample requests, enable storeless mode + request-hash + ML redaction pipeline, set retention to 24 hours, and run 10k synthetic interactions. Priya will run a redaction report. if that passes, move to dedicated for prod.
[08:44] Priya: i'll propose a pilot config and a sample dataset template. also i'll include instructions to run a minimal bench to measure token throughput and latency with redaction enabled.
[08:55] Evan: curious about cost impact. does redaction or region lock materially change billing?
[09:01] Marcus: redaction compute is billed as part of inference pipeline; heavy redaction increases CPU and maybe adds per-request surcharge if it uses NLP models. region lock is a feature-level add-on for hosted and doesn't change per-token pricing but may change availability-based discounts. dedicated pricing is separate.
[09:15] Samir: we need to document all those options for procurement. please give a clear matrix of controls vs hosting mode.
[09:22] Marcus: will do. we'll send a matrix: hosted (pilot) vs hosted+region-lock vs dedicated vs private — controls, CMK, HSM, audit forwarding, SLAs.
[09:32] Maya: minor nit: some of our requests come from mobile clients with ephemeral IDs. can we disable IP/user-level logging to avoid reconstructing identities?
[09:42] Priya: yes you can opt out of IP logging and only keep an anonymized tenant id. there are trade-offs for debugging, but it's possible.
[09:50] Evan: for GDPR right-to-be-forgotten, if a user requests deletion, can Redwood delete all derived artifacts like embeddings or cached KV?
[09:59] Priya: we support deletions at tenant or request level; embeddings and KV caches can be evicted and embeddings storage can be purged. need to ensure downstream analytics also honor the deletion.
[10:10] Samir: any caveats for asynchronous copies (backups, snapshots)?
[10:14] Marcus: backups are included in retention windows; if you request deletion we will purge backups that are within legal safe bounds; some jurisdictions may require retaining data for a minimum time — we'll respect that.
[10:24] Evan: what's the typical turnaround time to produce an artefact for e-discovery? like full transcript export?
[10:29] Priya: for hosted pilot, usually 2-5 business days depending on size; dedicated/private can be quicker with direct access.
[10:36] Maya: are there tools to help with regulatory mapping? e.g., give us a mapping of gdpr articles and how Redwood features meet them?
[10:43] Marcus: yes we have a compliance mapping doc that ties features to GDPR/HIPAA/SOC2 controls. i'll attach it.
[10:49] Evan: are there any known gaps? we want to know where we might need compensating controls.
[10:54] Priya: common gaps for hosted: full CMK support in hosted, region-lock contractual guarantees without add-on, and tenant-level private networking; all solvable with dedicated/private. we'll surface those as part of the matrix.
[11:08] Samir: ok last legal question: if Redwood personnel need root access to investigate, what's the authorization flow?
[11:15] Marcus: we use Just-In-Time (JIT) access with approval flows; access is time boxed and audited. for enterprise we can require mutual NDA or on-site supervised sessions.
[11:25] Evan: good. thanks.
[11:28] Maya: can we run a quick scenario: developer posts prompt with an email and cc list, we want that email masked in stored logs — what's the sequence?
[11:35] Priya: sequence A: client-side pre-processing: mask email before send — zero risk. Sequence B: server-side ML redaction: request hits endpoint -> streaming inference -> redaction module runs on copy -> redacted copy stored; the original is transient in memory and never persisted. Sequence C: storeless: no content persisted, only request hash stored. each has tradeoffs.
[11:58] Evan: what if we need to support search over redacted content? can you index redacted tokens?
[12:04] Priya: you can index redacted placeholders or store metadata tags (entity types) for search without content. indexing real content requires stricter controls.
[12:13] Marcus: wrapping up — seems like pilot on hosted with strict storeless + ML redaction + 24h retention is acceptable to quartz to test feature fidelity. then migrate to dedicated for prod if controls meet audit.
[12:26] Samir: yes that's our preference. can you email the pilot config and the contract addendum options?
[12:31] Marcus: absolutely. we'll include region-lock add-on pricing and CMK/hsm options.
[12:36] Evan: one more — can we get a small threat model note about cross-tenant attacks for hosted so our risk team can review?
[12:42] Priya: yes, we'll include a short tech note and attack surface summary.
[12:46] Marcus: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the packet and pilot template. any final questions?
[12:52] Maya: none here.
[12:54] Samir: no. thanks.
[12:56] Evan: thanks all.

Meeting close. Recap of agreed items: pilot on hosted storeless + ML redaction, 24h retention, Redwood to provide SOC2/compliance mapping, pilot config and bench, Quartz to share retention and e-discovery scope.
